The defaulting itself is the open A1/A6 defect class, not something this sidecar should lock in. payment_due_date IS asserted because the page prints it explicitly. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free-text summary that rewords every run ('Annual property tax charges for 2026.' vs '2026 property tax notice.'), excluded by the standing rule already recorded on recommend_240124_0001. It was asserted in error when this sidecar was scaffolded from only 3 replicates, all of which happened to agree. || billing_period_start_date RE-BASELINED '' -> '2026-01-01' on 2026-09-08 (user approved). The page DOES print the period: the payment stub reads 'JANUARY 1 TO DECEMBER 31, 2026' (CU markdown offset 4630), and billing_period_end_date '2026-12-31' -- already asserted here and passing 9/9 -- is read from the second half of that same line, so the old '' made this the only sidecar in the corpus asserting a period with an end and no start. Sibling property_abbotsford prints 'For the period January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026' and already asserts the same pair, its extract twins at 0.953/0.924. The original '' was a GPT-5.2 artefact: pre-upgrade the value was '' 6/6 (and on 2 of those the start extract collapsed onto 2026-12-31 and was blanked by the span guard); GPT-5.5 reads the range correctly 9/9. CAVEAT -- this value rides on the GENERATE twin at 0.578, below the 0.73 bar: billing_period_start_date_extract grounds on the span 'JANUARY 1' and returns nothing, because it does not apply its own prompt's year-carry rule (the year is printed once, at the end of the range). So the key is model-sensitive and could go red again if CU is retuned; that would be a real signal, not a false failure. || service_address RE-BASELINED '2790 167 ST SURREY BC V3Z 0A9' -> '2790 167 ST' on 2026-09-08 (user accepted the shorter form). The new value is the MORE faithful one: the notice prints '2790 167 ST' under its own 'PROPERTY ADDRESS' label (markdown offset 618) and again as 'CIVIC' on the payment stub (offset 5535); the city and postal code appear only in the MAILING block at offset 406 ('LYU SHUWEN / XUE LI / 2790 167 ST / SURREY BC V3Z 0A9'), which is the owner's mail-to, not the serviced property. The old assertion spliced the property-address line together with the mailing block's city/postal. Measured on the upgraded model: resolved '2790 167 ST' 9/9, with service_address_extract returning it on EVERY replicate at 0.925-0.959, far above the 0.73 bar; the only 2 reads where the generate twin appended the city sat at 0.413, below the bar. Routing is HAPPY_PATH_CANDIDATE 9/9 either way, so this is not a routing change. service_address stays asserted -- it is base-critical and must never be dropped to make the corpus green; this re-baselines the value, it does not remove the coverage. The written record loses city/province/postal for this document family; that is the normalisation question DV-4 already owns. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice. || account_number is written WITHOUT the 'Account No: ' prefix on this family (user requirement, 2026-09-09, propertytax ONLY -- every other municipal bill and every commercial invoice keeps the label). The written value is the bare folio, which is what an owner quotes to the municipality. || RAW-READING ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-14 (user authorised, all 54 sidecars): the corpus checks only written values (writeValues) and routingDecision, never a raw CU extract/generate reading.
